correctness.rationale: A fixed annular phase-canceling test produces a constant nonzero output. After frequency dilation, the normalized logarithmic phase converges smoothly to log|eta|, whose Hessian has one negative radial and d-1 positive tangential eigenvalues, all nonzero. Uniform stationary phase therefore gives the input norm with exponent d(1/p-1/2) for p>2. The localized operator norm grows as the claimed logarithmic power. Global boundedness would uniformly bound these localizations, and adjoint duality gives p<2. At equality the proof yields only a constant lower bound, so no unsupported endpoint conclusion is made.
